## New product development
In business and engineering, new product development (NPD) or simply product development is the complete process of bringing a new product to market. Product development also includes renewing an existing product and introducing a product into a new market. New product development is the realization of a market opportunity by making a product available for purchase. The products developed by a commercial organization provide the means to generate income. A central aspect of NPD is product design.
Many technology-intensive organizations exploit technological innovation in a rapidly changing consumer market. A product can be a tangible asset or good or intangible services or user experiences. NPD requires an understanding of customer needs and wants, the competitive environment, and the nature of the market.
Cost, time, and quality are the main variables that drive customer needs. Aiming at these three variables, innovative companies develop continuous practices and strategies to better satisfy customer requirements and to increase their own market share by regular development of new products. There are many uncertainties and challenges which companies must face throughout the process.

## Living+
"Living+" is the sixth episode of the fourth season of the American satirical comedy-drama television series Succession, and the 35th episode overall. It was written by Georgia Pritchett and Will Arbery and directed by Lorene Scafaria, and originally aired on HBO on April 30, 2023.
Succession centers on the Roy family, the owners of global media and entertainment conglomerate Waystar RoyCo, and their fight for control of the company amidst uncertainty about the health of the family's patriarch Logan (Brian Cox), who has passed away by this point of the series. The episode sees the Roys preparing the launch of "Living+", Logan's unrealized initiative on Waystar's Investor Day, as the ambition of Kendall (Jeremy Strong) and the unresolved grief of Roman (Kieran Culkin) threaten to destabilize the company. The episode notably features Cox's first appearance since Logan's death three episodes prior in "Connor's Wedding", as Logan appears via videos he had recorded for the launch.
“Living+" received critical acclaim, with praise for the performances (especially from Strong, Sarah Snook and Matthew Macfadyen), direction, and satirical elements. The episode earned Primetime Emmy Award nominations...

## Marketing communications
Marketing communications (also known MC, marcom(s), marcomm(s) or just simply communications) refers to the combined use of different marketing channels and tools. Marketing communication channels focus on how businesses communicate a message to their desired market, or the greater market in general. It can also include the internal communications of the organization. Marketing communication tools include advertising, personal selling, direct marketing, sponsorship, communication, public relations, social media, customer journey, and promotion.
MC are made up of the marketing mix which is made up of the 4 Ps (Price, Promotion, Place and Product), for a business selling goods, and made up of 7 Ps: Price, Promotion, Place, Product, People, Physical evidence and Process, for a service-based business.

## Social video marketing
Social video marketing is a component of an integrated marketing communications plan designed to increase audience engagement through social activity around a given video. In a successful social video marketing campaign, the content, distribution strategy and consumer self-expression tools combine to allow an individual to “add their voice” or co-create value to a piece of content - then further disseminate it out to their social acquaintances. Social video typically benefits from a halo effect cast by the "influencers” of a given social grouping. Social video marketing draws on consumer-culture theory, economic theory, and social theory around the psychology of sharing. Social video marketing differs from social marketing, which has the intent of influencing behavior for a social good.
Media publishers and content rights holders create social videos from TV, live video feeds and pre-recorded content in order to generate engagement on social platforms and drive media distribution. They use real-time video editing software to instantly create and share social videos in native formats such as vertical video for Snapchat and square video for Instagram. ## Tutorial
In education, a tutorial is a method of transferring knowledge and may be used as a part of a learning process. More interactive and specific than a book or a lecture, a tutorial seeks to teach by example and supply the information to complete a certain task.
A tutorial can be taken in many forms, ranging from a set of instructions to complete a task to an interactive problem solving session (usually in academia).

## Concept video
A concept video, also known as an "explainer video", is a marketing tool used to promote, describe and explain technological services (such as consulting), or products (such as apps), to individual consumers and other businesses (i.e. business to business). They may be released as part of a social media campaign, or used exclusively between the buyer and seller of the product. Concept videos may be developed in-house by the producer of the product, or by a third-party marketing company.

plan.title: A Note-Taking App That Finds Your Ideas Again
plan.description: A launch video for a note-taking app built around fast capture, instant search and easy sharing. See how it keeps your ideas in one place so you can find them when you need them.

beats.narration: You wrote it down. You were sure you would find it later. Now it is buried under sticky notes, screenshots, and half-finished lists. Finding an idea should never take longer than having it.

props.alt: colorful sticky notes on a wall

beats.narration: So we built a note-taking app to help you capture and find your ideas. Here is how it works, from the first word to the last search.

props.title: Capture fast. Find instantly.
props.subtitle: A note-taking app that keeps every idea within reach

beats.narration: Here is the problem. An idea arrives. You jot it in a notes app, snap a photo in another, and text yourself a reminder. Soon your thoughts are lost in several places, and none of them talk to each other.
Capture comes first. Open the app and you land on a blank page, cursor already blinking. Type, speak, or paste a photo. There are no folders to pick and no setup before you start writing.
Most great ideas arrive away from the desk. On a train, during a walk, in the middle of a meeting. Your notes should be ready whenever they show up.
Then organization happens for you. Tag a note once, and it links to related ideas. Notes about a trip sit beside your packing list. Projects gather their own pages without any dragging.
Now the moment that matters: finding it. Type a word you half remember, and look for the note you need.

props.text: Find any note while you are still typing.

beats.narration: Notes are not only for you. Sometimes an idea is worth sharing with a teammate, a classmate, or a friend.

clip_queries: friends planning a trip with map

beats.narration: Compare the two. Before, notes sit in scattered places, searching means scrolling, and sharing means copying and pasting. After, everything lives in one place, search is instant, and sharing is a single link.
Your notes should be there when you need them. So the app works offline on a plane, syncs across your phone and laptop, and keeps your writing private to you by default.
Getting started is quick. First, download the app. Second, create your account. Third, write your first note, and watch it appear on every device you own.
Think of what a notebook of ideas becomes over a year. Plans that happened, lists that saved a weekend, thoughts you almost lost. A good note is a small promise to your future self.

props.alt: hands writing in a notebook at a desk

beats.narration: Your best idea is only useful if you can find it. Start writing today.

props.text: Your best idea is only useful if you can find it.

hook_close.hook_text: You wrote it down. You were sure you would find it later. Now it is buried under sticky notes, screenshots, and half-finished lists. Finding an idea should never take longer than having it.
hook_close.close_text: Your best idea is only useful if you can find it. Start writing today.

accuracy.reason: The notes contain no product facts, and the script invents specifics as if real: offline mode, sync, private by default, auto-linking, instant search, a single share link, voice capture. None are flagged as placeholders, and the app has no name.

coverage.reason: It has a problem, solution and benefit arc with a call to action, but the feature descriptions are generic, there is no differentiator, no named app, and the search beat is thin ("Type a word you half remember").

structure.reason: The order is clear: problem, capture, organize, find, share, trust, start, close. The chapters help. Beats 2 and 3 are slightly out of order, because it promises a walkthrough and then returns to the problem.

hook_ending.reason: "You wrote it down. You were sure you would find it later." is a relatable opener. The closing line is a tidy tagline, but it repeats the title and the kinetic text, and "Start writing today" is a weak call to action.

tone.reason: The voice is warm, consumer-friendly and confident, which suits a launch video for a US audience.

visuals.reason: The scene types vary (clip, diagram, icons, versus, checklist, steps). Each matches its narration, and the versus table suits a before/after comparison. Beat 7 is only text and is weak, and beats 5 and 12 are generic stock.

originality.reason: Lines like "A good note is a small promise to your future self" are nice, but the features and framing are standard note-app marketing.

instructions.reason: It is a launch video of roughly the right length, but it presents invented features as fact, without placeholders or hedging, against the note's guidance.

language.reason: The prose is clean and fluent. Some lines are repetitive, such as "capture and find your ideas" and "Your best idea is only useful if you can find it".

missing: App name and a concrete call to action
Placeholders or hedging for unconfirmed features
A specific differentiator against Apple Notes, Notion and similar apps
wrong_facts: Offline, sync, private-by-default, voice capture and auto-linking are unverified product claims, with nothing in the notes to support them.
judge.summary: The script is well structured, warm and visually varied, with a clear problem-solution-CTA arc. However, it asserts invented features as fact, never names the app, and treats its central search feature thinly.
